Add 影絵 (kagee), a 3D shadow-matching puzzle with a theatre world

Third game: rotate a block figure in 3D by dragging or with arrow keys
until its shadow on the screen matches the dotted outline. A match of
90% or more raises the curtain and names the shadow; near-exact poses
snap into place. Figures are built from the target silhouette, so every
act is solvable. 20 acts; act 1 needs only left-right turns and act 2
only up-down, each with a tutorial hint and arrow.

The garden slides gain a third world (velvet curtains, spotlight, linen
screen; Rampart One and Zen Kaku Gothic New). Shares the one-screen game
layout, help dialog and completion panel. Cache: hirameki-v9.
Tests cover selection, drag, keyboard solve, persistence, next act,
one-screen fit and light/dark contrast. Docs updated for three games.

One-screen game screens, help dialogs, first-level tutorials

Both games now share a one-screen layout: back link, compact header
(name, help, sound, level), a stage that scales the board to the
remaining space, and a footer where the completion panel replaces the
move bar. Rules move from on-screen text into a help dialog. Level 1 of
each game is a tutorial that highlights the next tile or star pair and
explains one rule at a time. Hoshizu switches to Kaisei Decol.

Tests check the one-screen fit at six viewport sizes for the first and
largest levels, the help dialog and the tutorial. Cache: hirameki-v8.
README, DESIGN_RULES and WORK_LOG record the shared game-screen rules.

Hoshizu: keep the night world in dark mode and switch to Zen Maru Gothic

On devices in dark mode, garden.css's dark-scheme :root rule outranked
the hoshizu variables, so the night screens fell back to the washi
background and the pale text vanished into it. Raise the hoshizu
variables' specificity, brighten secondary text and enlarge small type.
Replace Shippori Mincho B1 with Zen Maru Gothic for legibility, including
the star numbers. Tests now check the hoshizu background and text
contrast (>= 4.5) in both light and dark schemes. Cache: hirameki-v7.

Add 星図 (hoshizu), a bridges puzzle with its own night world

Second game: connect stars with light lines (Hashiwokakero). 30 nights
from 5x5 to 9x10, generated by tools/hoshizu-gen.cjs and kept only when
the solution is unique. Tap two stars, drag from a star, tap a line to
cycle 1/2/0, or use Shift+Arrow; crossings are refused. Undo, two-step
reset, completion, next night and best moves, saved separately from
kintsugi.

The garden title gains a slide switcher (arrows, names, swipe, keys)
that swaps the whole title into the chosen game's world and remembers
it; the world is set before first paint so the opening's final light
matches. The night world uses a drawn starfield, a brass star-chart
plate and Shippori Mincho B1.

Cache bumped to hirameki-v6. Tests cover the new game and slides;
existing selectors now target the kintsugi screen. README,
DESIGN_RULES, CLAUDE.md and WORK_LOG describe the two-game garden.

Fit the garden home screen on one screen

Lock the garden to the viewport height and let the ceramic art absorb
the remaining space so the title, game card and play button are always
visible without scrolling. Phones drop the longer copy and footer,
portrait tablets stack art above text, and only very short screens fall
back to scrolling. Hide the focus ring on the programmatically focused
title. Bump the cache to hirameki-v4; tests check the one-screen fit.

Play the opening when the app opens to the title

Add opening.js/opening.css and load them from index.html. The opening
plays only on a fresh load of the title (not when returning from the
game, opening at #kintsugi, or with reduced motion), starts from a
sound/mute choice, can be skipped by button or Escape, and fades into
the title's own background colour. The final white-light sound is now
half as loud. Fonts are fetched as text subsets after their CSS loads.

sw.js caches the new files (hirameki-v3). Tests cover the opening and
two existing checks now wait for the screen switch they assert on.
README, DESIGN_RULES and WORK_LOG document the behaviour and fonts.
